key_findings: SinglePrompt learned 10-prompt selection is nearly indistinguishable from random selection in its CIFAR100 routing ablation, while a single prompt is smaller and slightly better in that stripped comparison.

Removing SinglePrompt minibatch label masking collapses CIFAR100 A_auc/A_last from 85.58/87.53 to 65.57/51.81 and raises F_last from 5.89 to 48.19; the mechanism is supervised label-local negative-gradient suppression, not label-free drift handling.
The apparent paper batch-size 32 versus script batchsize 64 discrepancy is not a defect: the trainer sets stream temp_batchsize=batchsize//2=32; buffer mode adds a separate 32-example replay batch.
SinglePrompt buffer experiments use reservoir replacement plus uniform random replay, so their gains do not depend on a specialized replay selector.
